passages.text: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889. It was built as the entrance arch to the 1889 Exposition Universelle in Paris, on the Champ de Mars. The fair marked the centenary of the French Revolution.

Engineers Maurice Koechlin and Émile Nouguier produced the first design in 1884, while working for Gustave Eiffel's company. Architect Stephen Sauvestre later added decorative arches to their proposal. Eiffel then presented the revised project to the exposition commissioners.

The tower remained the world's tallest man-made structure until the Chrysler Building in New York surpassed it in 1930. It had held that record since it was finished. The Chrysler Building's spire was completed in May 1930.

A group of prominent artists published a protest against its construction in the newspaper Le Temps in 1887. They called the planned tower a useless and monstrous structure. The signatories included painters, writers, and composers.
Eiffel first offered the design to the city of Barcelona. Barcelona did not take up the project. The tower was later built in Paris for the exposition.

The tower is repainted roughly every seven years to protect its iron from rust. A full campaign uses about sixty tonnes of paint. The shade of the paint has varied slightly from one campaign to the next.
The tower was meant to stand for only 20 years under the original permit. It was kept after that term because it became useful for radio transmission. Demolition plans were dropped.

extra_passages.text: Around 7 million people visit the Eiffel Tower each year, and it is often described as the most visited paid monument in the world. The operating company counts ticketed entries. The exact figure changes from year to year.
